rationale: Masking is relational. A soloed spectrum cannot determine which source should move or whether the conflict is primarily level, arrangement, or frequency.

recommended_first_experiment.action: First lower bass slightly. If that reveals tom fills, restore the fader and test a small broad cut on bass in the overlap while preserving low-end continuity.
recommended_first_experiment.summary: First lower bass slightly. If that reveals tom fills, restore the fader and test a small broad cut on bass in the overlap while preserving low-end continuity.
recommended_first_experiment.why_this_first: It is intended to distinguish likely causes before adding more processing or making a permanent move.

starting_points: Search the actual overlapping notes/phrases rather than using a generic frequency chart.
Prefer the smallest broad move that clarifies the role.
stop_rule: Stop when both roles are legible; do not force complete spectral separation.
teaching_principle: Solve masking with the cheapest relationship change first: level, arrangement, then frequency.
title: Unmasking tom fills and bass
tradeoffs_and_risks: Complementary EQ can become formulaic and hollow.
A static cut may be unnecessary when the overlap is intermittent.
undo_or_reset: Restore the competing-source fader and bypass the diagnostic bands.
what_to_listen_for: Tom Fills should retain fill weight; bass should retain low-end continuity.
The relationship should improve without sounding carved apart.
